title: Run the test check with cargo-nextest to cut suite run time
summary: Goal: faster Athena checks, CI and producer test loops, judged by the user reading docs/decisions.md and later job times. Per the user's measurements (compile 67 s, run 673 s), adopt a pinned cargo-nextest for the test check, CI and producer guidance, with `cargo test --doc` run separately so every test still runs. If nextest can't be installed, fall back to splitting the slowest binaries.

defaults_applied.how: Adopt cargo-nextest instead of building a parallel test runner; record alternatives.
Decision entry cites the measured split and labels the unmeasured after-median.
Criteria check that every test still runs and failures still fail the check.
cargo test, clippy and fmt stay clean.
The check is enforced in athena.toml and CI, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Compile/run split numbers (67 s vs 673 s on 4 cores) are taken from the user's reply and recorded as measured by the brain.
The test check in athena.toml (both change and study) becomes nextest plus a separate doctest step, which may need a check-list entry or a wrapper command.
Producer and verifier command allow-lists need 'nextest' added as a cargo subcommand so the new check and guidance work.
Pinning follows the existing [tools] pattern (e.g. gitleaks) by version and checksum; nextest is installed in CI and Athena's check environment the same way.
After-change median cannot be measured in this job; the decision states how it will be measured on later jobs and claims no after number.
Audience: the user and the later verifier reading docs/decisions.md, athena.toml and CI.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/decisions.md has a new decision recording the measured split (compile 67 s via cargo test --no-run, run 673 s warm, 4 cores, measured by the brain, with the slowest binaries listed), the chosen change (cargo-nextest plus cargo test --doc), and at least three alternatives (sccache per D79, shared target dir, splitting slow tests) with reasons.
The decision states the before medians (9.7 min checks, 17.6 min producers, 29 jobs) and how the after median will be measured on later jobs; it claims no unmeasured after number.
athena.toml [tools] pins cargo-nextest by version and checksum like the other tools, and the test check (change and study) uses nextest plus a separate doctest run, with no test filtered or ignored.
.github/workflows/ci.yml installs the pinned nextest and runs nextest and cargo test --doc, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry with the measured split.

Run `cargo test --locked`: it passes clean with about 1190 tests, so a failing test still exits non-zero; the check definitions in athena.toml and CI are read to confirm a nonzero nextest or doctest exit fails the check.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: both clean.

out_of_scope: Adopting sccache or a shared target directory
Measuring the after-change median in this job
departures: Touches CI, tool pinning with checksums and command allow-lists, and nextest may not be installable in the sandbox, so slightly lower pass odds and higher cost than the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts the median check time (9.7 min) and producer test waits, reducing timeouts and wasted time per job.
